findings.summary: D5 says a cancelled or stopped probe parks nothing and logs it, but in production it does park: the real ProcessLauncher never throws on cancellation. It still starts agy, kills it, and returns TimedOut=true with Cancelled=true (ProcessLauncher.cs:481-527, ResultOf:570). AgyQuotaProbe.Reading reads that as 'timed out after 30 s', so a Spent==true refusal is parked on its stated text with a false note, and the OperationCanceledException catch in QuotaCooldowns.AfterRoundAsync never runs. S42 cannot see this because its fake launcher (TheRoundParksAndLiftsTheQuotaTests.cs:220-231) throws TaskCanceledException, which the real launcher never does. The round's token also carries the round deadline and host stop (RoundEngine.cs:294, 442), so this happens on every round that ends that way.
findings.fix: In AgyQuotaProbe, do not launch when ct is already cancelled. Treat result.Cancelled as cancellation, not as a timeout: throw, or return a reading that parks nothing and logs 'cancelled'. That is how GitHistory.cs:324, WorkRangeReader.cs:109 and ReviewTreeRoot.cs:172 already read Cancelled. Make S42's fake answer the way the real launcher does (TimedOut: true, Cancelled: true), or have S42 use the real ProcessLauncher, and see it go red before the fix.

findings.summary: No test exercises the engine's call to QuotaCooldowns.AfterRoundAsync, the one line that makes a round park or lift anything. Every S22-S25/S34/S41/S42 test calls AfterRoundAsync directly, and only those four test files mention QuotaCooldowns, so deleting this line leaves the suite green. research/module_tests.md still lists 'the round's park and lift' as covered.
findings.fix: Add a test through PanelService/RoundEngine. Run a round in which a scripted reviewer ends with a spent refusal, then assert that ExcludedFrom for the next stage names the row with this side's sentence, and that a later round's Ok lifts it. Delete line 442 and watch the test go red.

findings.summary: D5 says a key qualifies for parking when ANY of its outcomes is Spent==true, or is Spent==null and hopeless by its words. Refusal() instead takes the first undecided refusal regardless of whether it is hopeless. Example: two rows on one key (codex or kimi), the first a transient '429 Too Many Requests' and the second 'You've hit your usage limit'. The first is chosen, QuotaReset.OfText answers NotParked, and the spent quota is not remembered; with a sibling Ok the key is even lifted.
findings.fix: Order undecided refusals by RateLimit.Hopeless(reason) after Spent==true, or ask ReadResetAsync for each candidate until one parks. Add a scenario with both refusals in either order.

findings.summary: The computed public properties UntilIso (line 58) and QuotaName (line 73) of QuotaCooldownEntry are written to quota-cooldowns.json. A scratch script that called Park against the built assembly produced a file with "untilIso" and "quotaName" (here 'quota for some-model on Antigravity (group unknown)'). That is two fields beyond D4's seven-field schema, and the extra size grows with the model id, against §8's per-entry budget.
findings.fix: Mark both properties [JsonIgnore], or move them off the persisted record, so the file holds exactly key, untilUtc, source, model, note, sinceUtc and consecutive.

findings.summary: S40's 'fraction negative' and 'fraction above one' rows cannot fail. With the [0,1] range check in AgyQuotaReport.Fraction removed, -1 and 2 are still not == 0, so the group answers Available either way. The rows do not prove D6's 'unreadable and skipped' rule.
findings.fix: Build those rows so that skipping changes the answer: set both Gemini buckets to -1 (or 2) and expect GroupMissing, which reads Available without the check. Confirm by removing the range check and watching the rows go red.
